age_seconds.description: Age of the data at response time

as_of.description: When the data was read from the ledger

ledger_index.description: Validated ledger the data comes from

stale.description: True when served past its fresh TTL (stale-on-error)

peg.description: Currency the stablecoin is pegged to

source_url.description: The issuer's own documentation for this stablecoin

canonical.description: True when the asset is in the closed registry of canonical stablecoins

canonical_issuer.description: The canonical issuer of that currency code when `impersonation_risk` is true; else null

impersonation_risk.description: True when the currency code is a registry code but the issuer is not its canonical issuer

allow_clawback.description: The issuer may claw back issued balances

global_freeze.description: The issuer has frozen every trust line of its currencies

no_freeze.description: The issuer gave up its freeze powers for good

require_auth.description: A holder needs the issuer's authorization to hold the token

transfer_fee_pct.description: Issuer transfer fee as a percentage, a decimal string (`0` when there is none)

posture.description: The live issuer or mint facts, read now; null when the asset is not canonical or its account is missing

posture_differences.description: Every fact that changed since the snapshot, as `<field>_changed`, or `issuer_not_found` or `mint_not_found` when the canonical account is missing; empty when they match and when the asset is not canonical

posture_matches_registry.description: True when every live fact equals the recorded snapshot; null when the asset is not canonical

registry_entry.description: The registry entry: symbol, peg, issuer name and the issuer's documentation URL; null when the asset is not canonical

snapshot_date.description: The date the recorded snapshot was read; null when the asset is not canonical

description: Is this XRPL issued currency the canonical stablecoin it claims to be? When to use: Before accepting or quoting a stablecoin: to check the asset is the canonical one and that its issuer facts have not changed since the snapshot. Prefer another tool: To read supply or balances (use `/v1/xrpl/token/{asset}` or `/v1/xrpl/account/{address}/lines`), or as a regulatory or licensing check: none is served. Example: xrpl_stablecoin {"asset":"4555524F50000000000000000000000000000000.rMkEuRii9w9uBMQDnWV5AA43gvYZR9JxVK"} Credits only: paid by prepaid credit, 0.0005 EUR or 0.0006 USD units per call; buy a bundle first at https://api.criptonlabs.com/v1/pro/credits/{bundle} or with `credits_topup`, then call with the `clc_` token or Sign-In-With-X.

asset.description: Issued asset, never XRP. Currency format: `XRP`, or `CODE.issuer`: `CODE` is a 3-character standard code or 40 hexadecimal digits, and `issuer` is a classic XRPL address. Standard codes are case-sensitive: `usd` and `USD` are different tokens, so send the exact code. A standard code uses letters, digits or `?!@#$%^&*<>(){}[]|` and is never `XRP`; percent-encode the symbols in a URL (for example `%3F` for `?`). A 40-hex code is read in any case, and the 40-hex form of a standard code means that code.
